extra.message: Open redirect: the `next` query parameter is read from request.args and passed directly to flask.redirect() with no validation. A URL such as /toggle_xss_protection/?next=https://evil.com redirects the victim to an attacker-controlled site, enabling phishing and OAuth/token-theft attacks.

extra.message: Missing authentication: MessagesView.post (POST /api/v1/messages) has no @admin_required (or any auth) decorator, unlike the other methods in the class. Any unauthenticated user can create Message records with arbitrary, fully attacker-controlled `message` and `from_user` fields, which are then rendered unsanitized in the admin panel (stored XSS) and listed by the admin-only index endpoint.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: CSRF on password change: /account_area/change_password is a state-changing POST endpoint that relies solely on the flask_login session cookie for authentication and has no CSRF token (Flask-WTF/CSRF is not enabled anywhere). A malicious site can forge a cross-origin POST that changes the victim's password, enabling account takeover.

CSRF on email change: /account_area/change_email is a state-changing POST endpoint authenticated only by the session cookie with no CSRF protection. A cross-site forged POST can change the victim's email address.

CSRF on send_feedback: /account_area/send_feedback is a state-changing POST endpoint authenticated only by the session cookie with no CSRF protection. A forged cross-site POST can submit feedback (stored messages) on behalf of the victim, which is also the injection vector for stored XSS in the admin panel.

Login CSRF: /auth/login accepts POST without any CSRF token/anti-CSRF measure. An attacker can forge a cross-origin POST to log the victim into the attacker's account (login CSRF), enabling subsequent credential theft via synced data.

Hardcoded Flask SECRET_KEY: 'Keep it secret, keep it safe' is committed in source. Flask signs session cookies with this key; anyone who knows it can forge a valid session cookie (e.g., setting user_id to the admin's id) and bypass authentication entirely, achieving full account/admin takeover.

Default admin password: the add_admin management command defaults password='admin', and the admin user's privileges are granted based on username == 'admin' (app/models/models.py:20-21). Combined with the login page hint, this yields a trivially guessable admin/admin credential pair for the most privileged account.

Plaintext password storage: User.password is stored as a plain String column with no hashing. This is confirmed by direct equality comparison at app/blueprints/login/views.py:17 (user.password == password) and the update at app/blueprints/account_area/views.py:34-36 which writes the new password verbatim. A database compromise exposes every user credential directly, and reused passwords leak across sites.

When served via the development server this enables the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which can permit remote code execution (e.g., via the debugger console) and leaks detailed stack traces and source code on errors.

extra.message: Improper authorization: administrator privileges are granted solely by `self.username == 'admin'` rather than a dedicated role/flag. Privilege is therefore derived from a well-known, guessable string and the unique username constraint becomes the only access-control boundary for the most powerful account.
